workflow_hypothesis: Link-time optimization produces an out-of-range branch
pattern: Target-specific LTO code generation exceeds a branch encoding range
description: An LTO-enabled build on a target architecture produces assembly whose branch displacement cannot be encoded, causing the toolchain to reject an intermediate executable.
precondition: A build enables link-time optimization on a target/toolchain combination that encounters a branch-range limitation.
critical_operation: The toolchain performs LTO code generation while linking an intermediate executable.
interference: Generated assembly contains a branch whose target is outside the encodable range.
invalid_assumption: The build assumes the target toolchain can complete LTO code generation for this executable without violating branch-encoding constraints.
failure: The assembler rejects the out-of-range branch; the LTO wrapper and linker then fail, aborting the build.
search_strategy: Check whether link-time optimization is enabled for targets with known branch-range or code-layout limitations.
Rebuild the failing link without link-time optimization to isolate toolchain-generated code from source-level failures.
Inspect LTO-generated assembly and assembler diagnostics for out-of-range branch instructions.
Verify that the compiler, assembler, and linker versions support LTO on the affected target architecture.
Add a target-specific build probe for successful LTO linking of a representative large intermediate executable.

evidence.supports: An LTO-enabled build on a 64-bit target fails while linking an intermediate executable because the assembler reports a branch out of range; removing LTO makes the build succeed.

scope_note: Singleton cluster. The report supports an LTO-dependent, target-toolchain branch-range failure, but does not establish a particular optimization pass, layout algorithm, or source-code cause.
